Subject: SLA template: uptime anchoring & monthly remedy proposal

Alex —

Following our call last week, attached is a refreshed SLA template that reflects the production characteristics you described (batched inference, scheduled regional maintenance windows). High level:

- Provisional uptime anchor: 99.95% for the first 90 days post-go-live to account for the batched-warmup behavior we saw in the POC.
- After the 90-day stabilization window we revert to the standard 99.99% anchor (or we can agree a phased ramp to 99.97% / 99.99%).
- Monthly remedy: credits calculated on shortfall bands (see attachment SLA_Calculation_Scenarios.xlsx) with a cap at 50% of monthly invoice for exceptional months.
- Maintenance carveouts: up to 6 hours/month scheduled maintenance (regional) are explicitly excluded; emergency remediation windows will be treated case-by-case.

I included two files: SLA_Template_Redwood_v3.docx (editable redlines) and SLA_Calculation_Scenarios.xlsx (three worked dollar examples based on MRR levels you provided).

Next steps: could you confirm whether procurement needs a flat-dollar cap instead of percentage cap? If so we can convert the worked examples into a fixed-dollar cap for your MRR. Also loop in anyone from legal you want us to sync with — happy to take redlines.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Alex / team —

Looping in from CS/legal to propose language that bridges your procurement ask and our operational posture. Key points below and in the attached redline: SLA_Template_Redwood_v3.docx (see tab "Legal - Camila redlines").

Proposal (counter):
- Production uptime anchor: 99.97% (steady state).
- Stabilization window: first 90 days post go-live set to 99.95% as Camila suggested.
- Remedy calculation: credit = min( (monthly invoice) * f, cap ), where f is the shortfall ratio per band: 
  * 99.97 - 99.90 => 10% of monthly invoice
  * 99.90 - 99.00 => 25% of monthly invoice
  * <99.00 => 50% of monthly invoice
  We can convert the cap to a fixed-dollar cap for NimbleHealth; based on your numbers the 50% cap equates to ~$42,500 in month 3 (we used $85k as MRR).
- Fixed-dollar cap option: we can replace percentage caps with a fixed cap of $45,000/month for months where your invoice is >$80k; below that we use the percentage model (keeps small-months proportional).
- Maintenance carveouts: 6 hours/month scheduled maintenance per region; multi-region rollouts that cause overlapping impact will be treated as scheduled only if proactively notified 14 days in advance and accepted by Redwood operations. Emergency/force majeure are excluded per standard contract language.

We will prepare a DocuSign-ready version once we agree on the fixed-dollar cap vs percentage approach. Karthik — please speak to whether the 6-hour window should be extended for migration events (he can advise ops tradeoffs).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
